title: The Fox and the Cat
paragraphs: It so happened that the cat met the fox in a forest. She thought to herself, “He is clever and experienced, and highly regarded in the world,” so she spoke to him in a friendly way. “Good day, dear Mr Fox. How are you? How is everything with you? How are you getting along in these hard times?” The fox, puffed up with every kind of arrogance, looked the cat over from head to foot, and for a long while couldn’t decide whether to answer at all. At last he said, “Oh, you miserable whisker-washer, you spotted fool, you starving mouse-hunter, what are you thinking? How dare you ask how I’m getting along? What have you learned? How many arts do you know?” “I know only one,” replied the cat humbly. “What art is that?” asked the fox. “When the hounds are chasing me, I can spring up a tree and save myself.” “Is that all?” said the fox. “I’m master of a hundred arts, and on top of that I have a sackful of tricks. I feel sorry for you. Come with me, and I’ll teach you how to get away from the hounds.” Just then a hunter came along with four dogs. The cat leaped nimbly up a tree and sat at the very top, where the branches and leaves hid her completely. “Open your sack, Mr Fox, open your sack!” the cat called down to him, but the dogs had already caught him and were holding him fast. “Ah, Mr Fox,” cried the cat, “with all your hundred arts, you’ve been left in the lurch! If you could have climbed like me, you wouldn’t have lost your life.”
